Report Title Slide.report_title: General Corporate Operations - Payroll and Timekeeping Controls

Objective, Background and Scope.purpose_objective: Assess payroll and timekeeping control environment including timesheet approvals, payroll calculation accuracy, reconciliation processes, and segregation of duties to ensure payroll integrity and accurate financial reporting.
Objective, Background and Scope.background: Payroll is a high-volume, high-risk process. Recent organisational changes included an interim payroll processor and an upgrade to the timekeeping system in 2025; controls should ensure continuity and accuracy during transitions.
Objective, Background and Scope.scope: Review included testing of timesheet approvals for the most recent payroll cycle (sample 60 entries), review of monthly payroll reconciliations for the last six months, and assessment of segregation of duties over payroll initiation and vendor payments.

Overall Internal Audit Rating.overall_conclusion_description: Payroll controls are generally established but application gaps were noted in approval and reconciliation processes, creating moderate to high residual financial and operational risk which requires corrective actions.

Observation Slides.details: Testing of 60 employee timesheet records from the most recent payroll cycle identified 9 records (15%) where timesheets were processed without documented managerial approval prior to payroll cut-off. Evidence: timesheet export dated 2026-01-31 and payroll processing logs.
Observation Slides.risk_impact: Processing timesheets without prior approval increases risk of incorrect payments and potential payroll fraud. This weakens control over pay accuracy and employee entitlement verification.
Observation Slides.recommendations: 1) Enforce system controls to prevent payroll processing of unapproved timesheets. 2) Implement a pre-payroll exception report and require documented escalation for late approvals. 3) Conduct retraining for managers on approval timelines.
Observation Slides.management_response_action_plan: Payroll will configure the timekeeping system to block unapproved timesheets and implement a pre-payroll exception report. Remediation owner: Payroll Manager (Lydia Harper). Target date: System configuration and exception reporting implemented by 2026-03-15; manager retraining completed by 2026-04-15.

Observation Slides.observation_title: Payroll Reconciliation Variances Not Timely Resolved
Observation Slides.details: Review of monthly payroll reconciliations for the six most recent months found 3 months with unresolved reconciling items totaling $18,450 (net) outstanding for more than 30 days. Supporting investigation documentation was incomplete for two of the months. Evidence: reconciliation workbook and bank statements for July-December 2025.
Observation Slides.risk_impact: Unreconciled payroll items increase the risk of incorrect financial reporting, potential duplicate payments, and delayed detection of errors or fraud, potentially impacting financial statement accuracy.
Observation Slides.recommendations: 1) Establish SLA of 10 business days to resolve payroll reconciling items with documented root cause analysis. 2) Require monthly reconciliation sign-off by Finance Controller. 3) Enhance monitoring of reconciliation aging and escalate items beyond SLA.
Observation Slides.management_response_action_plan: Finance will formalise reconciliation SLAs and require Controller sign-off; outstanding items will be investigated and cleared. Remediation owner: Head of Finance Operations (Samantha Lee). Target date: SLA and sign-off process effective by 2026-03-31; outstanding reconciling items cleared by 2026-04-30.

Report Title Slide.report_title: General Corporate Operations - Vendor Management and IT Access Controls

Objective, Background and Scope.purpose_objective: Evaluate controls around vendor onboarding/management and IT user access provisioning to ensure vendor risk, payment integrity and logical access controls mitigate operational and information security risks.
Objective, Background and Scope.background: Third-party vendors and IT user access are critical to operations. Weak vendor due diligence or excessive IT privileges can create fraud, data leakage and continuity risks. Previous internal reviews highlighted gaps in vendor validation and access recertification.
Objective, Background and Scope.scope: Review covered vendor onboarding and master data management processes for vendors added between 2024-01-01 and 2025-12-31 (sample 25 new vendors) and IT access provisioning for 50 user accounts across finance and operations. Included review of vendor master changes, contract documentation and access entitlement lists.

Overall Internal Audit Rating.overall_conclusion_description: Significant deficiencies found in vendor due diligence and IT access controls, leaving the organization exposed to financial, operational and data security risks. Immediate remediation is required to tighten onboarding, approval workflows and access recertification processes.

Observation Slides.observation_title: Insufficient vendor due diligence and missing contract documentation
Observation Slides.details: In a sample of 25 newly onboarded vendors, 11 (44%) had incomplete due diligence: 7 lacked third-party validation (no W-9/Tax ID or equivalent), and 4 had no signed contract on file despite invoices being paid. Total paid to these 11 vendors during the review period was $1,250,000. Absence of contracts for $420,000 in spend was noted.
Observation Slides.risk_impact: Increased exposure to duplicate/fictitious vendors, tax withholding errors and contract non-compliance leading to potential financial loss and legal exposure. Absence of contracts for $420,000 in spend creates recovery and SLA enforcement risk.
Observation Slides.recommendations: Enforce mandatory vendor documentation before activation: tax forms, AML screening and signed contracts. Implement hold-back policy preventing payments for vendors without validated documentation. Centralize vendor master with workflow approval and periodic duplicate vendor detection.
Observation Slides.management_response_action_plan: Procurement will enforce 'no pay' activation rule and implement mandatory vendor checklist in the vendor onboarding system. Target date: 2026-05-31. Remediation owner: Procurement Director, Omar Patel. Procurement and AP to reconcile vendor master and complete missing documentation for the 11 vendors by 2026-04-30.

Observation Slides.observation_title: Excessive IT access privileges and lack of periodic access recertification
Observation Slides.details: From a review of 50 user accounts, 18 accounts (36%) held privileges inconsistent with role-based least privilege principles (e.g., finance clerks with payroll admin rights). No evidence of formal access recertification for these users in the last 12 months. One user account showed remote VPN access despite separation requirements.
Observation Slides.risk_impact: Excessive privileges increase risk of data manipulation, unauthorized transactions and data exfiltration. Lack of recertification increases residual access risk; potential impact includes unauthorized changes to payroll or vendor records.
Observation Slides.recommendations: Implement role-based access control (RBAC) model and enforce least-privilege assignments. Conduct mandatory access recertification semi-annually for critical systems. Disable dormant accounts and enforce MFA for remote access.
Observation Slides.management_response_action_plan: CISO to implement RBAC pilot for Finance and Operations and schedule first recertification sweep. Target date for RBAC pilot: 2026-06-30. Remediation owner: CISO, Laura Martins. MFA rollout for remote access to be completed by 2026-05-15; recertification process to be executed starting 2026-06-01.

Objective, Background and Scope.purpose_objective: Assess design effectiveness and operating efficiency of procurement processes across corporate functions, including adherence to procurement policy, competitive sourcing, vendor selection, and contract approval controls.
Objective, Background and Scope.background: Procurement activity represents significant operational expenditure and is a key control area for cost management, vendor risk mitigation and regulatory compliance. The organization updated its Procurement Policy in 2025; management requested an audit to validate implementation and identify residual control gaps.
Objective, Background and Scope.scope: Fieldwork covered procurement transactions and controls from 2025-07-01 to 2025-12-31. Testing included: evaluation of procurement policy enforcement, review of 25 sample contracts above $10,000, due diligence on 20 newly onboarded vendors, and assessment of approval workflows and contract repository completeness.

Overall Internal Audit Rating.overall_conclusion_description: Procurement controls are partially effective. Key policy enforcement and vendor due diligence processes are inconsistently applied resulting in exposure to procurement fraud, supplier concentration and contractual liability. Management has begun remediation but gaps remain. Two observations were identified requiring prioritized action.

Observation Slides.details: Procurement Policy requires documented competitive bids for purchases above $10,000. In a sample of 25 contracts > $10,000 executed in the review period, 7 (28%) lacked documented evidence of competitive bidding or written justification for single-source procurement. Supporting documentation was missing in the contract repository for 5 of these 7 transactions.
Observation Slides.risk_impact: Increases risk of supplier favoritism, overpayment, and reduced value-for-money; potential regulatory and reputational exposure related to non-compliant procurements.
Observation Slides.recommendations: Enforce mandatory competitive bidding workflows for contracts > $10,000, implement electronic approval gates that prevent PO issuance without required bid documentation, and maintain a centralized, searchable procurement register recording bid evaluation and awarding rationale.
Observation Slides.management_response_action_plan: Procurement will update the SOP to require electronic bid evidence and implement a procurement register integrated with the ERP. Training for procurement staff and approvers will be completed. Target date: 2026-03-15. Remediation owner: Procurement Director, Jane Doe.

Observation Slides.observation_title: Incomplete vendor due diligence and onboarding records
Observation Slides.details: In a sample of 20 new vendors onboarded in 2025, 9 (45%) had incomplete due diligence files: 6 lacked tax registration documents and 5 lacked documented conflict-of-interest attestations (2 overlap). The vendor master data in ERP lacked documentation links for these vendors.
Observation Slides.risk_impact: Exposes organization to regulatory non-compliance, potential tax liabilities, and increased third-party risk including transaction with sanctioned or conflicted parties.
Observation Slides.recommendations: Implement a mandatory checklist that prevents vendor activation in ERP until required due diligence artifacts are uploaded. Conduct a retrospective remediation on all vendors onboarded in 2025 and suspend payments to vendors with unresolved documentation until cleared.
Observation Slides.management_response_action_plan: Vendor Management will deploy a vendor activation workflow in the ERP requiring mandatory document uploads and will run a clean-up project to remediate 2025 onboardings. Retroactive remediations will be completed by 2026-04-01. Remediation owner: Vendor Management Lead, Carlos Mendez.

Report Title Slide.report_title: General Corporate Operations - Cash Management and Expense Controls

Objective, Background and Scope.purpose_objective: Assess design effectiveness and operating efficiency of cash management and employee expense controls to determine adequacy of procedures, segregation of duties and compliance with corporate policy.
Objective, Background and Scope.background: The corporate treasury and accounts payable functions manage daily cash positioning, disbursements and employee expense reimbursements. Effective controls are required to mitigate fraud, misstatement and regulatory non-compliance. Prior internal audits noted control weaknesses in these areas.
Objective, Background and Scope.scope: Fieldwork covered cash disbursements, bank reconciliations, petty cash, and employee expense reimbursements for the period 2025-01-01 to 2025-12-31. Sample testing: 30 bank reconciliations (monthly), 40 cash disbursement transactions, and 30 employee expense claims across all business units.

Overall Internal Audit Rating.overall_conclusion_description: Control environment exhibits control design but inconsistent operating effectiveness leading to increased residual risk for unauthorized disbursements and policy non-compliance. Management has implemented some mitigations but additional remediation is required to reduce exposure to financial loss and regulatory risk.

Observation Slides.observation_title: Inadequate segregation of duties in cash disbursement workflow
Observation Slides.details: In a sample of 40 cash disbursement transactions, 10 (25%) were processed where the same individual initiated the payment request, approved the release in the ERP and executed the bank transfer. System roles permit combined 'Initiate/Approve/Execute' rights in 3 user accounts. Documentation shows only ad-hoc compensating reviews. One unsupported payment of $7,500 was identified during testing.
Observation Slides.risk_impact: Concentration of duties increases risk of unauthorized or fraudulent payments and misstatement of cash balances. Potential financial loss observed: one unsupported payment of $7,500.
Observation Slides.recommendations: Restrict system roles to enforce segregation: separate Initiator, Approver and Payment Execution roles. Implement four-eyes approval for disbursements above threshold $5,000. Configure automated approval workflows and enable audit logging with periodic review.
Observation Slides.management_response_action_plan: Treasury will reconfigure ERP role matrices and implement segregation of duties controls. Target date: 2026-04-30. Remediation owner: Head of Treasury, Jane Alvarez. Implementation includes role change, testing and retraining. Quarterly review of audit logs to be assigned to Internal Controls Analyst starting 2026-05-15.

Observation Slides.observation_title: Non-compliance with expense policy and insufficient supporting documentation
Observation Slides.details: In a sample of 30 employee expense claims, 8 claims (27%) lacked required original receipts or had receipts exceeding policy per diem limits. Total value of non-compliant claims: $6,420. Approval stamps were missing on 5 of these claims and 3 claims were approved after payment date.
Observation Slides.risk_impact: Increases likelihood of payroll/expenditure inaccuracies, potential tax/reporting issues and reputational risk. Weak documentation undermines ability to recover or justify VAT and other tax recoveries worth approximately $1,120 in the sample.
Observation Slides.recommendations: Enforce policy through system validation requiring receipt upload prior to approval. Introduce flagging for late approvals and automated query workflow for incomplete claims. Provide refresher training and update expense thresholds where justified.
Observation Slides.management_response_action_plan: Finance Operations to configure expense module to require receipt upload and implement automated flags for missing documentation. Target date: 2026-03-31. Remediation owner: Finance Operations Manager, Mark Chen. Training session for employees and approvers scheduled by 2026-04-15.

Report Title Slide.report_title: IT Access and Change Management Controls

Objective, Background and Scope.purpose_objective: Evaluate the effectiveness of logical access controls and change management processes supporting critical corporate systems to ensure confidentiality, integrity and availability of corporate data.
Objective, Background and Scope.background: IT access and change controls are fundamental to preventing unauthorized system access and production incidents. Recent organizational growth increased the number of privileged accounts and system changes, prompting review of access provisioning, privileged account management, and formal change control.
Objective, Background and Scope.scope: Testing covered identity and access management, privileged account reviews, and change management for production systems between 2025-07-01 and 2025-12-31. Samples included 40 privileged accounts, 60 regular user accounts, and 15 production changes deployed during the period.

Overall Internal Audit Rating.overall_conclusion_description: Access and change management controls are weak and not operating effectively. Multiple instances of excessive privileged access and non-compliance with change control procedures were identified, representing significant operational and information security risk. Immediate remediation is required.

Observation Slides.observation_title: Excessive privileged access and lack of periodic access reviews
Observation Slides.details: In a sample of 40 accounts with administrative privileges across core systems, 16 (40%) belonged to users whose roles did not require such privileges (e.g., finance analysts, HR coordinators). No evidence of quarterly privileged access reviews for these systems was available for 2025.
Observation Slides.risk_impact: Increases likelihood of unauthorized data modification, data loss, and potential segregation-of-duties violations contributing to fraud or system compromise.
Observation Slides.recommendations: Immediately revoke unnecessary privileges, implement role-based access controls (RBAC), and institute mandatory quarterly privileged access reviews with attestation evidence retained. Use automated access recertification and logging for privileged actions.
Observation Slides.management_response_action_plan: CIO will conduct a privilege entitlement review and remove non-essential admin rights within 30 days, implement RBAC and automate quarterly recertifications by 2026-03-31. Remediation owner: CIO, John Smith.

Observation Slides.observation_title: Production changes deployed without formal approval or test evidence
Observation Slides.observation_owner: Head of IT Operations, Maria Lopez
Observation Slides.details: In a sample of 15 production changes deployed in 2025, 6 (40%) lacked a formal change request record or test sign-off (3 lacked both). Root-cause analysis and rollback plans were not documented for 4 of these changes.
Observation Slides.risk_impact: Uncontrolled changes increase risk of production outages, data corruption, compliance breaches and extended business disruption due to lack of rollback or testing.
Observation Slides.recommendations: Enforce a change gate that prevents production deployment without an approved change request and attached test evidence. Require documented rollback plans and post-implementation reviews for all high-impact changes.
Observation Slides.management_response_action_plan: Head of IT Operations will implement deployment automation that checks for approved change tickets and test artifacts, require rollback plans for high-impact changes, and perform a retrospective audit of 2025 deployments. Target date: 2026-04-15. Remediation owner: Head of IT Operations, Maria Lopez.

Report Title Slide.report_title: Corporate Travel and Expense Controls Review

Objective, Background and Scope.purpose_objective: Assess the operating effectiveness of travel and expense (T&E) policies, approval workflows, expense reimbursement timeliness, and corporate card reconciliation to ensure expense integrity and policy compliance.
Objective, Background and Scope.background: T&E is a frequent control area for cost leakage and policy exceptions. The organization updated its travel policy in 2024 and introduced an automated expense management tool in 2025. Management requested validation of operating effectiveness post-implementation.
Objective, Background and Scope.scope: Testing covered expense reports and corporate card reconciliations from 2025-01-01 to 2025-12-31. Samples included 50 employee expense reports, 10 corporate card accounts and review of pre-trip approval evidence for business travel.

Overall Internal Audit Rating.overall_conclusion_description: Controls over travel and expenses are generally adequate with evidence of policy adherence and automated workflows reducing manual errors. However, isolated lapses in pre-trip approvals and delays in card reconciliations were identified and should be addressed to strengthen operating effectiveness.

Observation Slides.observation_title: Policy exceptions and delayed approvals for business travel
Observation Slides.details: Policy requires pre-trip approval for international travel and submission of expense reports within 60 days. In a sample of 50 expense reports, 12 (24%) either had no evidence of pre-trip approval (7 cases) or were submitted more than 60 days after trip completion (5 cases). Of the 7 without pre-trip approvals, 3 involved international travel.
Observation Slides.risk_impact: Lack of pre-trip approvals increases the risk of unapproved expenditures and travel that does not comply with safety or policy considerations. Late submissions hinder timely expense validation and may obscure inappropriate claims.
Observation Slides.recommendations: Enforce system checks that require pre-trip approval for international travel before booking, implement auto-reminders and escalation for expense reports older than 45 days, and consider a cap on reimbursements for reports submitted after 90 days unless exceptions are approved by Finance.
Observation Slides.management_response_action_plan: Head of Finance - Travel will enable pre-trip approval enforcement in the travel tool and configure auto-reminders and escalations by 2026-04-01. Remediation owner: Head of Finance - Travel, Emily Carter.

Observation Slides.observation_title: Delayed corporate card reconciliations and unreconciled transactions
Observation Slides.details: Corporate card reconciliations are required monthly. In a sample of 10 corporate card accounts, reconciliations for 4 accounts were completed with a delay exceeding 30 days on at least two occasions during 2025. Additionally, 3 accounts had unreconciled transactions totaling $8,450 as of the reconciliation date.
Observation Slides.risk_impact: Delayed reconciliations increase the risk of billing errors going unnoticed, fraudulent charges, and late payment fees. Unreconciled transactions may indicate control lapses in expense verification.
Observation Slides.recommendations: Institute KPI targets for reconciliation timeliness (e.g., complete within 15 days of statement) with monthly reporting to Finance leadership, require cardholders to reconcile within the travel tool and escalate persistent delays to line managers, and investigate and clear all unreconciled items within 30 days.
Observation Slides.management_response_action_plan: Treasury will implement monthly reconciliation KPIs and reporting, require reconciliation within 15 days, and complete clearance of outstanding items by 2026-03-20. Remediation owner: Treasury Manager, Ahmed Khan.
